statuses.label: Qualified or judged
statuses.description: Numerically qualified (a registered protocol passed) or judged (used in a registered experiment), in its declared scope.

statuses.label: Implemented and guarded
statuses.description: On main with its tests and guards: the plan's 'implemented' and 'guarded' levels. Not yet qualified by a registered protocol.

statuses.label: Established
statuses.description: Built earlier and in routine use: older model families and shared infrastructure. Scope and evidence are in each guide.

statuses.label: Designed
statuses.description: A design or protocol is written or accepted; the code is not on main.

statuses.label: Planned
statuses.description: Named in the plan or roadmap; not started.

statuses.label: Failed qualification
statuses.description: Built, then failed its registered qualification. Kept as evidence and not relied on.

statuses.label: External reference
statuses.description: Outside the engine: a reference simulator or data set, run out of process and compared through saved outputs.

representations.label: Simulated
representations.description: The engine evolves this state step by step, with material, charge and energy accounted for.

representations.label: Modelled in aggregate
representations.description: Represented as a population, count or rate law, not as individual molecules. Shapes drawn for it are illustrations.

representations.label: Prescribed
representations.description: Happens on a schedule the experiment sets; the cell does not decide it.

representations.label: Illustration only
representations.description: Drawn for orientation. Nothing in the engine stands behind it yet.

model_groups.label: Composite tissue model
model_groups.description: resolved_pump_composite@1: the pump tissue model's own step plus declared operators. These parts run together in one model today.

model_groups.label: Earlier tissue families
model_groups.description: The older resolved-tissue families, one module per feature combination. Calcium, fuel, mitochondria, regulation and repair run together here.

model_groups.label: Separate engines
model_groups.description: Models that run on their own: protein-cage assembly, vertex mechanics and the regulatory circuits.

relation_kinds.label: writes

relation_kinds.label: provides

relation_kinds.label: reads

relation_kinds.label: wraps

relation_kinds.label: runs

relation_kinds.label: would extend
relation_kinds.description: A planned or designed part, and what it builds on.

relation_kinds.label: delivers

relation_kinds.label: has its law in

relation_kinds.label: is drawn in the cell view as

proteins.title: Protein atlas
proteins.summary: The molecular machines Cells models: its own inventory, linked to the public protein atlases.
proteins.caveat: Shapes are schematic, drawn from subunit counts, and not to scale. A grey form is a generic law: no protein is assigned.

mappings.label: Assigned in source
mappings.description: The law, its documents or the source it cites names the protein. This records a label; the kind of evidence on each law says what stands behind it.

mappings.label: Candidate
mappings.description: The law models a named native current or channel class. Which gene products carry it is the inventory's inference.

mappings.label: Generic
mappings.description: The law is deliberately generic, phenomenological or manufactured. Products are listed as candidates only.

evidence.label: Expressed isoform
evidence.description: The cited data come from the named isoform, expressed on its own.

evidence.label: Isoform named in the title
evidence.description: The cited source names the isoform in its title; the inventory read no further detail.

evidence.label: Native current
evidence.description: The cited data are a current recorded from native cells, not from an isolated isoform.

evidence.label: Neuron model
evidence.description: The cited source is a model of a neuron.

evidence.label: Derived reduction
evidence.description: A reduced (Morris-Lecar) form of the named channel.

evidence.label: Designed protein
evidence.description: An engineered protein with no natural gene product.

evidence.label: No detail in the source
evidence.description: The source gives no detail on what the coefficients were measured from.

entities.label: CPU, float64
entities.plain: Every model runs on ordinary processors in double precision. These runs are the reference that GPU runs are checked against.

entities.label: NVIDIA L4 GPU
entities.plain: One GPU runs many independent worlds at once. All 12 BETSE parity protocols also pass on it, under registered GPU variants.

entities.label: Ensemble workers
entities.plain: Workers take batches of independent simulations from a shared queue, one persistent process per GPU.

entities.label: JUPITER GH200
entities.plain: A supercomputer allocation of 10,000 GPU-hours. The recipe and runbook are ready; nothing has run there, and its speed is unmeasured.

entities.label: One world across GPUs
entities.plain: Splitting one large interacting tissue across several devices. No code does this; it is added only if single-device measurements justify it.

entities.label: Command line
entities.plain: The command that runs a model from a configuration file and writes its results and checkpoints.
entities.detail: Command line: validate, run, resume, and explicitly branch a saved world.

entities.label: Definitions
entities.plain: Each run is declared as data: the model, the experiment and how to execute it. Definitions are checked before anything runs.

entities.label: Model registry
entities.plain: Finds the model code for a definition. Today it is an ordered chain of type checks.
entities.detail: Small explicit model registry: no dynamic plugins or organ-name branches.

entities.label: Declarative registry
entities.plain: One table saying how each model takes part in parsing, saving, controls, execution and checkpoints.

entities.label: State and resources
entities.plain: State is held as explicit arrays with fixed capacities and masks; memory needs are estimated before a run starts.
entities.detail: Array state is separate from biological identity and host scheduling state.

entities.label: Schedules and phases
entities.plain: Timed changes an experiment makes, such as blocking a pump or a junction, applied at exact times.
entities.detail: Host-side, right-continuous experiment controls; never physical fluxes.

entities.label: Single-world runner
entities.plain: Runs one world step by step with every check, in bounded windows. A reference path.
entities.detail: Host schedule + pure JAX rollout, with observations outside the dynamics.

entities.label: Guarded batch
entities.plain: Runs many independent worlds, each on its own clock, with rows checked on the host.
entities.detail: Independent worlds on their own clocks, using guarded compiled mapping.

entities.label: Batch windows
entities.plain: Runs cohorts of worlds in bounded rounds, with complete cohort checkpoints.
entities.detail: Bounded independent-clock rounds on the existing guarded batch kernel.

entities.label: Vector windows
entities.plain: Advances many worlds as one vectorised batch with the checks on the device. The candidate for the one production path.
entities.detail: Independent worlds advanced as one vectorized batch, with checks on the device.

entities.label: One production path
entities.plain: Naming one execution path for production and declaring the others as reference paths, with shared admission and checkpoint checks.

entities.label: Compile policy
entities.plain: A rule for what is compiled into a program and what is passed in, with a budget for compile time and memory.

entities.label: Run-view output
entities.plain: Every run will save what a viewer needs to replay it: geometry, identities, record metadata, events and how each layer is represented. The requirement is recorded (D154); its design note comes first.

entities.label: Device placement
entities.plain: Says explicitly whether work runs on a CPU or a GPU.
entities.detail: Explicit execution placement; CPU and GPU may coexist in one process.

entities.label: Checkpoints and files
entities.plain: Saves complete checkpoints, so a run can restart exactly or branch into alternative futures.
entities.detail: Portable numeric artifacts, strict restoration, and non-overwriting output.

entities.label: Checkpoint continuity
entities.plain: Lets a checkpoint written by one version of the code resume under another, but only through a recorded admission. Refusal stays the default. In place for CPU runs; the GPU extension is being built.
entities.detail: Checkpoint continuity: one recorded admission per resume across a source change.

entities.label: Observers
entities.plain: Read-only measurements taken from a run. Observing never changes the dynamics.
entities.detail: Read-only observation of already accepted numerical states.

entities.label: Tissue preparation
entities.plain: Prepares a tissue before an experiment and hands its full state to the next phase, with no silent re-equilibration.

entities.label: Cell removal
entities.plain: Cuts cells out of a tissue and continues the run, keeping the surviving material and its history.

entities.label: Other core modules
entities.plain: Core modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

entities.label: Checked RK4
entities.plain: A fixed-step integrator that checks every trial state and refuses a failed step; it never repairs one.
entities.detail: Classical RK4 over a PyTree; the caller fixes inputs within each segment.

entities.label: IMEX step
entities.plain: The tissue models' time step, treating the fast electrical part implicitly. It refactorises a dense matrix every step, which limits tissue size.
entities.detail: Linearly implicit face electromigration for the resolved capacitor field.

entities.label: Field solvers
entities.plain: Solve for the voltages that keep charge consistent across membranes and the space between cells. Limited to 2,048 electrical nodes today.
entities.detail: Charge-constrained membrane surfaces with coupled return currents and baths.

entities.label: Field-solver interface
entities.plain: An interface that keeps the field law and its checks while allowing sparse or matrix-free solvers. Proposed, with no code yet.

entities.label: Transport kernels
entities.plain: Shared array kernels for moving ions across membranes and junctions.
entities.detail: Resolved membrane surfaces and explicit open-compartment transport.

entities.label: Gate updates
entities.plain: Exact exponential updates for channel gates.
entities.detail: Exponential update of relaxation gates over a step whose voltage varies.

entities.label: Water step
entities.plain: The numerical step for water flow and volume change.
entities.detail: Conservative neutral-water exchange between finite compliant compartments.

entities.label: Membrane redistribution
entities.plain: Moves channels and pumps along the membrane while conserving their number.
entities.detail: Conservative lateral transport of membrane-bound populations on fixed patches.

entities.label: Projective stepping
entities.plain: A long-time mode that takes bursts of fine steps and then jumps ahead. It failed its qualification on the absolute error caps.
entities.detail: Projective forward Euler: coarse outer steps around a qualified fine integrator.

entities.label: Fixed points
entities.plain: Finds a tissue's resting states and follows them as parameters change. Passed all 16 criteria of its protocol.
entities.detail: stationary_continuation_analysis@1: stationary states and their stability.

entities.label: Long-time methods
entities.plain: Multirate or quasi-steady stepping for hours to months of biology. A verdict on them is a deliverable of the compute-limits gate.

entities.label: Mechanical analysis
entities.plain: Finds mechanical equilibria of a cell sheet and infers junction tensions from its shape. Qualified with the vertex model.
entities.detail: mechanical_equilibrium_analysis@1: equilibria, spectra and linear moduli of a vertex tissue.

entities.label: Other numerics
entities.plain: Numerics and analysis modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

entities.label: Membrane transport
entities.plain: Ions cross membranes driven by concentration and voltage, with each transfer counted once.
entities.detail: Pure dimensioned membrane laws, independent of layouts, schedules, and solvers.

entities.label: Channel catalogue
entities.plain: 56 sodium, potassium, HCN, calcium and leak channel laws. The heredity channels NaV1.2 and Kir2.1 pass BETSE parity.

sources.where: Parity P4b, the heredity carrier channels

entities.label: Pumps
entities.plain: The sodium–potassium pump and the calcium pumps, which spend ATP to move ions uphill.
entities.detail: Positive-domain 3 Na out / 2 K in ATPase with maintained metabolic pools.

entities.label: Gap junctions
entities.plain: Gated channels between neighbouring cells, and the law by which a new cell forms its junctions over time.
entities.detail: Continuous physical-time junction conductance from the BETSE v1.5.0 rate equations.

entities.label: Cotransport
entities.plain: Carriers that move two kinds of ion together, including the potassium–anion symport cells use to regulate volume.
entities.detail: Manufactured reversible electroneutral symport, without geometry or stepping.

entities.label: Reactions
entities.plain: Chemical reactions inside compartments, with mass and energy accounted for.
entities.detail: First-order reversible conversion between two explicitly supplied amount fields.

entities.label: Calcium and IP3
entities.plain: Calcium release from the ER store, IP3 signalling and calcium entry at the membrane.
entities.detail: Positive-domain BETSE 1.5 ER pump and instantaneous calcium release laws.

entities.label: Fuel and mitochondria
entities.plain: Finite pools of ATP that pumps draw on, and passive ion exchange with mitochondria. Respiration is not modelled.
entities.detail: Finite transformed ATP/ADP/Pi pools and an explicitly driven synthesis port.

entities.label: Network regulation
entities.plain: Rules that let ion levels and fuel regulate pumps, channels and junctions.
entities.detail: Local reaction-network control factors and ordered target writes, @1.

sources.where: Live network regulation of pumps, channels and junctions

entities.label: Injury and resealing
entities.plain: A membrane injury that leaks ions and reseals on a set schedule.
entities.detail: Prescribed, dimensionless patch damage; not an energy-supported repair law.

entities.label: Physiological noise
entities.plain: Random variation with explicit, repeatable random streams.
entities.detail: Physiological noise arithmetic with prescribed draws and stable-owner sampling.

entities.label: Tissue geometry
entities.plain: Builds cells as polygons with explicit volumes, areas and neighbours.

entities.label: Extracellular grid
entities.plain: A grid for ions and currents in the space around cells.

entities.label: Charged-surface backend
entities.plain: Array kernels for charge-consistent membrane surfaces.

entities.label: Vertex mechanics
entities.plain: The forces in a sheet of cells, from edge tension and area elasticity. Topology is fixed: cells cannot yet swap neighbours.
entities.detail: Apical vertex mechanics: geometry, energy, box stress and a step bound.

entities.label: Topology changes
entities.plain: Cells swapping neighbours, leaving the sheet and dividing within it, with ions, charge and energy conserved.

entities.label: Coupling out of the inventory
entities.plain: A species amount in the inventory sets how available a channel or junction is, so chemistry can change electrical behaviour. In design.

entities.label: Excitable tissue
entities.plain: General physics for tissue that carries a travelling electrical wave, to be qualified against cable theory. A design note comes first.

entities.label: Gene regulation in tissue
entities.plain: Gene networks that set how much of each protein is made, coupled to the tissue's physiology.

entities.label: Golgi and trafficking

entities.label: First bounded models
entities.plain: The first small models: one cell, a pair, a regulatory circuit and small graphs of cells. Each was accepted in its own bounded scope.

entities.label: Finite and spatial exterior
entities.plain: Models where the fluid outside cells is a finite, spatial inventory with its own ions and fields.

entities.label: Calcium and chemistry
entities.plain: Models of calcium stores, IP3 signalling and compartment chemistry, tested on synthetic cases.

entities.label: Resolved tissue families
entities.plain: The older design: one module for each combination of calcium, fuel, water, repair, profiles and interventions. Kept frozen on purpose.

entities.label: Apical vertex model
entities.plain: A two-dimensional mechanical model of a cell sheet. It passed 57 of 57 criteria under its second protocol, after the first judged run failed.
entities.detail: apical_vertex_mechanics@1: overdamped 2-D apical vertex mechanics, periodic tissue.

entities.label: Protein-cage assembly
entities.plain: Protein cages forming from folded subunits drawn from finite pools, with an experimental link to cell models. Folding itself is out of scope.

entities.label: Coherent cell model
entities.plain: One cell in which many processes share the same inventories and predict several measured responses.

entities.label: Integrated tissue unit
entities.plain: Mechanics, transport and the cell lifecycle together on changing geometry.

entities.label: First organ
entities.plain: The simplest useful organ, expressed as a data definition. The organ and species are not yet chosen.

entities.label: Coupled organs
entities.plain: Two or more organs linked through explicit transport and signalling.

entities.label: Operator contract
entities.plain: What every operator must declare: the state it owns, what it writes and reads, its energy bookings and its conflicts. Checked when a model is built.

entities.label: Endogenous lifecycle
entities.plain: Division triggered by a cell's own growth or regulation, with repeated births and deaths. Mitosis itself is further down the road.

entities.label: BETSE parity ladder
entities.plain: Cells' own physics compared with saved output from the BETSE simulator, one mechanism family at a time. Every family tested so far passes, on CPU and GPU.

entities.label: MG1: vertex mechanics

entities.plain: Prescribed division of the early frog egg, judged against independently written references. Stages through S5a passed.

entities.plain: Can the channel laws the composite admits carry an action potential along a chain of cells? A probe on the engine as it stands is in progress, with its success criteria set before it runs.

entities.label: BITSEY

entities.label: Membrane voltage
entities.plain: Ions cross the membrane and set its voltage, with every ion, charge and joule accounted for. Checked against the BETSE simulator.

entities.label: Ion channels
entities.plain: Channels open and close with the membrane voltage. Each kind is a population with gates, not individual proteins. The catalogue holds 56 laws. NaV1.2 and Kir2.1, the channels the heredity experiments use, pass the BETSE comparison; channel time constants are still open.

entities.label: Ion pumps
entities.plain: The sodium–potassium pump and calcium pumps move ions uphill and spend ATP. Each is a population with a rate law. The calcium pump's comparison passed on a second protocol, after the first failed on one item.

entities.label: Gap junctions
entities.plain: Neighbouring cells exchange ions through gated junctions, and a new cell forms its junctions over time.

entities.label: Space between cells
entities.plain: The fluid around cells holds its own ions and electric fields, with barriers between regions.

sources.where: Parity rungs P2 and P4 pass

entities.label: Water and cell volume
entities.plain: Water follows osmotic pressure, so cells swell, shrink and regulate their volume.

sources.where: Osmotic water and volume qualified and landed

entities.label: Calcium and the ER
entities.plain: Calcium moves between the cytoplasm and the ER store, with IP3-triggered release. Tested on synthetic cases.

entities.label: Fuel (ATP)
entities.plain: Pumps draw on a finite pool of ATP that has to be regenerated. In the composite model fuel is held constant.

entities.label: Mitochondria
entities.plain: Mitochondria exchange ions with the cytoplasm and carry their own voltage. Respiration and ATP synthesis are not modelled.

entities.label: Regulatory circuits
entities.plain: Small gene circuits that switch a cell between states, alone or in a two-cell model.

sources.where: What Cells can do: Regulatory cell state

entities.label: Gene regulation in tissue
entities.plain: Gene networks that set how much of each protein is made, coupled to the tissue. Planned.

sources.where: Where things stand: New biology in the engine

entities.label: Golgi and trafficking
entities.plain: New proteins would pass from the ER through the Golgi to the membrane or out of the cell. Planned, not started.

entities.label: Protein assembly
entities.plain: Protein cages build up from folded subunits drawn from a finite pool. Assembly is modelled as bonds forming and breaking, not as molecules moving in space. Folding is out of scope.

entities.label: Molecular machines
entities.plain: Larger machines such as the proteasome. A goal: they will mostly be modelled in aggregate and drawn as illustrations.

entities.label: Cell chemistry
entities.plain: Chemical reactions inside compartments, with mass and energy accounted for. Reactions on the tissue's shared inventory are implemented and guarded; their qualification is in progress.

entities.label: Secreted signals
entities.plain: Signalling molecules spread between cells and are cleared. That transport and clearance are numerically qualified in the composite model, with a held source (D150 v1). Release, uptake and production are implemented and guarded by tests, not yet qualified.

sources.where: Secreted-species transport (D150 v1) is numerically qualified

entities.label: Injury and repair
entities.plain: A membrane injury leaks ions and reseals. The resealing follows a set schedule.

entities.label: Cell division
entities.plain: A cell divides into two daughters on a set schedule, splitting its contents, membrane and channels with closed accounts. Division triggered by the cell itself is planned.

entities.label: Cell replacement
entities.plain: Cells are removed and replaced on a schedule, and newcomers form junctions over time. This is how the heredity experiments turn a tissue over.

entities.label: Tissue mechanics
entities.plain: Cells in a sheet pull on their shared edges and relax to mechanical equilibrium. Cells cannot yet swap neighbours.

entities.label: Cell sheets
entities.plain: A sheet of 127 coupled cells runs on ordinary processors today; the judged heredity experiment E07-v1 used it. The full tissue of 825 electrical nodes needs faster hardware or a long-time method.

entities.label: Molecules
entities.plain: Channels, pumps and protein cages are modelled as populations and counts, not atom by atom. Shapes drawn at this scale are illustrations.
entities.note: Assembly from prefolded proteins is mostly modelled, not simulated physically.

entities.label: One cell
entities.plain: The current focus: a coherent model of one cell, where many processes share the same inventories.

entities.label: Tissue
entities.plain: Sheets of coupled cells run today. An integrated tissue unit with mechanics and the lifecycle is a later gate.

entities.label: Organ
entities.plain: A first whole organ, defined as data. Planned; the organ and species are not yet chosen.

entities.label: Whole organism
entities.plain: Interacting organ systems, and in time whole animals. A long-term goal; nothing is built.
